title: Meridian Workstation Intrusion
description: Investigate a fake remote-support incident from initial access through persistence and lateral movement.
safety: The attacker domains and public IPs in this question set are fictional or documentation-range indicators. Do not resolve, browse to, or contact them.

questions.title: First host
questions.prompt: Which workstation was compromised first?
questions.hint: Which host first started a shell straight from Explorer?

questions.title: First user
questions.prompt: Which domain user ran the first suspicious process tree?
questions.hint: Check the user on the earliest suspicious process, not later logons.

questions.title: Initial access
questions.prompt: What social engineering technique got the user to paste and run the first command?
questions.hint: Look at the Run dialog history in the registry.

questions.title: Download
questions.prompt: Which command interpreter did Explorer start to download and unpack the first bundle?
questions.hint: Match the Run dialog history to processes started by explorer.exe.

questions.title: Loader file name
questions.prompt: What file name did the loader run under on disk?
questions.hint: What did tar.exe write?

questions.title: Loader identity
questions.prompt: What original file name is embedded in that executable?
questions.hint: Sysmon records the original file name from the binary's version info.

questions.title: Path configuration
questions.prompt: What Python path configuration file was placed next to the loader?
questions.hint: tar keeps the archive's file times, so check Sysmon event 2 as well as event 11.

questions.title: Startup code
questions.prompt: Which archive file supplied the loader's startup code?
questions.hint: Not every archive has an archive extension.

questions.title: First payload
questions.prompt: What executable did the loader start first?
questions.hint: Look at the loader's direct children.

questions.title: Discovery
questions.prompt: Which two built-in Windows programs were run over and over to collect user and network details?
questions.hint: Ignore anything launched through cmd.exe.

questions.title: System inventory
questions.prompt: Which parent and child pair collected operating system details? Submit them in order, parent first.
questions.hint: One of the two only wraps the other.

questions.title: Remote support tool
questions.prompt: Which remote support tool was deployed under the same support-themed file name?
questions.hint: Two different binaries share one file name. Compare their original file names.

questions.title: Typed command
questions.prompt: What command line did the attacker type to open a shell?
questions.hint: Look for a command a person typed, not the automated discovery.

questions.title: Trusted process
questions.prompt: Which legitimate program loaded a DLL from the user profile, started discovery commands and made an outbound connection?
questions.hint: Look at image loads from user-writable folders.

questions.title: Persistence
questions.prompt: What registry value was added for persistence? Submit the key path with the value name, starting with HKCU.
questions.hint: Sysmon names user hives by SID, not HKCU.

questions.title: Plugin DLLs
questions.prompt: Which two DLLs were staged in the user-writable plugin folder?
questions.hint: Look at every file written to the folder the DLL loaded from.

questions.title: Sprayed password
questions.prompt: What password was tried against several domain accounts? (case sensitive)
questions.hint: Look for command lines that pass a password.

questions.title: Rejected users
questions.prompt: Which two regular user accounts rejected the sprayed password?
questions.hint: Check failed Kerberos pre-authentication.

questions.title: Rejected admin
questions.prompt: Which admin-named account also rejected the sprayed password?
questions.hint: Same events as the last question.

questions.title: Working credential
questions.prompt: Which account accepted the sprayed password?
questions.hint: Look for a successful logon right after the failures.

questions.title: Second host
questions.prompt: Which workstation did the attacker move to?
questions.hint: Where did that account log on next?

questions.title: Movement tool
questions.prompt: Which remote service execution tool did the attacker use to move?
questions.hint: Search command lines on the first host for UNC paths.

questions.title: Admin shares
questions.prompt: Which two admin shares were used, one to test credentials and one to stage the payload?
questions.hint: Zeek's SMB mapping log records share names.

questions.title: Service name
questions.prompt: What service name was installed on the target?
questions.hint: System event 7045 records new services.

questions.title: Payload account
questions.prompt: Which account did the payload run as on the second workstation?
questions.hint: Check the user on the payload's process start, not the logon account.

questions.title: Attacker domains
questions.prompt: Which two attacker domains appear in the intrusion?
questions.hint: Rank DNS queries from the affected hosts and look for rare names.

questions.title: Domain to IP
questions.prompt: Which IP address did each attacker domain resolve to?
questions.hint: Check Zeek DNS answers.

questions.title: Implant port
questions.prompt: Which destination port did the implant use for command and control?
questions.hint: Separate the implant's traffic from the remote support tool's traffic.

questions.title: Remote support ports
questions.prompt: Which two destination ports carried the remote support tool's signaling and relay traffic?
questions.hint: Count only completed connections from the client. Ignore attempts that were never answered.

questions.title: Extra remote support port
questions.prompt: Which other destination port did the remote support tool connect to successfully?
questions.hint: Look at all of its connections, not only the long ones.

questions.title: Callbacks
questions.prompt: Which two workstations called back to the implant's server?
questions.hint: Use endpoint logs to confirm the source host.
